evidence_note: Brhat Parasara Hora Sastra read DIRECTLY IN SANSKRIT from the 1899 Subodhini edition (eGangotri digitisation of the Nepal Sanskrit University, Balmeeki Campus copy; djvu text at jyotisha/sources/bphs_subodhini_1899_djvu.txt, 1,106,274 characters, 807,038 of them Devanagari, 100 question marks in the whole file). A previous audit pass recorded this file as unusable ('near-total ? corruption'); that was wrong and is corrected in source_audit.md. The OCR is ordinary noisy Devanagari: ligatures are garbled in places, printed sloka numerals are occasionally misread (adhyaya 15 prints 84-86 as 87, 88, 86), and marginal furniture is mixed in - but the verse text itself is substantially readable throughout the purva-khanda and every quotation below was transcribed from it by eye. RECENSION WARNING, which this pack does not paper over: this is not the BPHS that modern readers know. Its own running headers and colophons call the first half 'Brhatparasarahorasaramsa' - the essence/abridgement of the Brhatparasarahora - the publisher's preface claims the work runs to a hundred adhyayas in two khandas (purva 51, uttara 80 by its own count) and states that it had never before been printed. The purva-khanda's chapter order (arudha at 11, upapada at 12, karakamsa at 9, rasi-drsti at 4) is Jaimini-inflected and does not match the Sharma or Santhanam recensions of the 20th century, which have different chapter counts, a different arrangement, and a good deal of material absent here. Where a cell is missing from this recension it is recorded as missing; material from the modern recensions is NOT imported to fill it. Every Devanagari quotation carries an engine_rendering graded 'engine_translation_unreviewed': no modern copyrighted translation was consulted or relied on as the authority, which is why the original is shown beside every rendering. customer_prediction is false on every conclusion in this file and no engine code consumes it. Clauses asserting the death, barrenness, unchastity, caste, foreignness or bodily incapacity of the native or of a third party are transcribed faithfully under restricted_by_house or restricted_clauses with output_policy 'refused' - retained as historical testimony about the text, never rendered as a claim about a living person, matching the treatment already used in the Byzantine and Sukuyodo packs. This pack is kept strictly separate from the Phaladeepika pack at jyotisha/delineation_rule_manifest.json: BPHS and Mantresvara are different authors of different dates and their results are never merged into one rule.

results_by_graha.Saturn: Saturn's excellent dasa produces splendour, discernment, sacrifices and such rites, fields and villages, leadership, much trade, and men skilful and eager.
results_by_graha.Rahu: Rahu's excellent dasa produces every kind of welfare, great royal fortune, enterprise, journeys to holy places, and the increase of knowledge and influence.
results_by_graha.Ketu: Ketu's excellent dasa produces victory, the gaining of wealth through fierce action, [favour of] a foreign ruler, fortune obtained, the beginning of undertakings, and the destruction of enemies.
